text:
Marathon Petroleum rose slightly today as oil prices stabilized after a Friday decline. The broader oil market fell on news of potential U.S.-Iran diplomatic talks aimed at de-escalating Middle East tensions—a development that eased fears of further supply disruptions from attacks on shipping and Saudi infrastructure. MPC recovered some ground from its steep drop earlier in the week (down nearly $33 from September 17 to September 22), though it remains well below that level.

The refining backdrop remains supportive: U.S. refineries are running at 94% capacity with diesel and gasoline inventories relatively tight, which typically benefits refiners' margins. However, political uncertainty around a potential diesel export ban—which could cut refiner production but might eventually raise fuel prices—adds an element of unpredictability to the outlook.
